title: WHEN GOD OPENS THE MOUTH OF A DONKEY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn, either to the right or to the left. When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, it lay down under Balaam, and he was angry and beat it with his staff. Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and it said to Balaam, "What have I done to you to make you beat me these three times?" - Num 22:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Trapped in the narrow place, the donkey simply lies down. Balaam, furious, beats it again. And then something astonishing happens: the Lord opens the donkey's mouth, and it speaks. The animal asks Balaam why he has beaten it three times.

This is one of the strangest moments in all of Scripture, and it is meant to arrest us. God can use even a donkey to speak His truth. If the Lord chooses, the most unlikely voice can become His messenger. Balaam, the renowned prophet, is being rebuked by his own beast of burden.

There is humbling wisdom here. God is not limited to the channels we expect. He can bring correction and truth through the humblest means, even through those we consider beneath us. Our pride tells us we know better, but God delights to confound the wise through the lowly (1 Cor 1:27).

Be careful never to despise the voice God may use to reach you. It might come through a child, a stranger, a simple believer, or a circumstance you would rather ignore. The God who opened a donkey's mouth can speak to you in unexpected ways. The question is whether you are humble enough to listen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you willing to receive truth from unexpected or humble sources?
2. Does pride ever make you dismiss the voices God might use?
3. Who might God be using to speak to you right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, humble my heart to hear Your truth, even from the most unexpected voices. Keep me from pride that dismisses the messengers You choose to send. Amen.
